findings.title: Layered barriers to contact
findings.claim: The pericope sets an outer screen between reciter and listeners beside coverings over the heart and weight in the ears, so the focus's blocked comprehension is pictured across interpersonal, cognitive, and auditory points of contact.
findings.mechanism: The concealed screen in 17:45 supplies an obstacle between people; the focus then places coverings over hearts, names failure to comprehend, and locates heaviness in ears. Their contact changes an inward-only defect into a layered interruption of access, while the two distinct s-t-r nominations are kept apart: concealment survives, the intermediary-person sense does not.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the focus moves from blocked understanding to burdened hearing: the interruption is already framed as relational and then reaches inward.
findings.containment: This is an image-level sequence, not a claim about three literal devices or one physical causal chain. The focus's ordinary account of covered hearts, ear-weight, and aversion remains intact; a parallel-metaphor reading remains possible.

epistemic.reason: The channel support directly supplies the 17:45-to-17:46 barrier relation, while the represented HFT trace adds the outer-layer formulation with legacy_unbound attribution.

findings.title: Repeated disclosure and recoil
findings.claim: What could look like one reaction to the Lord's exclusive mention becomes one turn in a repeated reception pattern: 17:41 gives Quranic presentation the aim of remembrance, yet names increased flight, and 17:60 places a test and warning beside increased transgression.
findings.mechanism: The focus's Quran and flight meet the same Quran-and-flight pattern in 17:41; the focus's mention also meets that ayah's remembrance verb from the same root. In 17:60, a test and warning are followed by another increase construction. These contacts make the focus response part of a pericope sequence in which repeated address meets an intensified response, while leaving open whether the address produces or only exposes that direction.
findings.reader_payoff: The contrast between intended remembrance and growing recoil becomes visible, and the focus's turning away reads as part of repeated encounters rather than an isolated reaction.
findings.containment: The supplied sequence supports recurrence and increased response, not proof that revelation itself causes refusal or that precisely the same individuals are involved at each point. A live alternative is that each disclosure exposes a refusal already increasing.

epistemic.reason: The focus and selected contexts verify the relevant roots, surfaces, and coordinates, but the feedback relation and its direction remain an attributed HFT inference.

findings.title: The collapse of an intermediary network
findings.claim: The focus's 'your Lord alone' moves beyond an abstract statement of oneness when read among the pericope's dependent figures: imagined gods seek a route toward the Throne, those invoked seek their Lord, and those people are told cannot remove harm or change it. The recoil can therefore register a threatened hierarchy of patrons and access.
findings.mechanism: The focus's Lord and alone terms carry exclusive sovereignty; the proposed gods' route-seeking and the invoked beings' own seeking independently make those figures dependent, while 17:56 denies them control when called. Their contact shifts the recoil from a response to oneness in abstraction toward resistance to the loss of an intermediary network's endpoint status.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive why exclusivity has social force in this passage: the beings who might mediate access are themselves dependent and unable to deliver relief.
findings.containment: The pericope supports a relation among imagined gods, invoked beings, and the one Lord; it does not identify every historical patron or prove this network is each hearer's motive. A narrower response to numerical plurality remains live.

epistemic.reason: The stated context coordinates and roots are supplied, while the claim that this hierarchy explains the recoil remains the legacy_unbound HFT's attributed inference.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The named Lord is the endpoint on which the proposed intermediaries depend.

findings.title: Uncomprehended praise in a speaking creation
findings.claim: 17:44 says that all things glorify God with praise yet its addressees do not grasp that glorification; the same f-q-h root meets the focus's blocked comprehension. The focus therefore shifts from one unread recitation to a parallel failure to recognize praise-bearing discourse already present around the hearers.
findings.mechanism: The focus's understanding term meets the context's explicit 'you do not understand' occurrence, while the surrounding glorification and praise supply meaningful signal. That contact changes the scale of the obstruction: the focus's covers operate beside a context in which the created order praises, even as that praise remains uncomprehended.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the barrier as a failure to grasp meaningful discourse in abundance, not simply a missing or silent message.
findings.containment: The adjacent ayat support a parallel of non-comprehension; they do not equate cosmic glorification with Quranic recitation or explicitly identify the same audience. The two failures may remain distinct.

epistemic.reason: The exact context and matching f-q-h occurrences are supplied, but their extension into one selective interpretive incapacity is an attributed contextual inference.

findings.title: Hearing followed by social recoding
findings.claim: The focus's ear-weight could be read as keeping the Quran from arriving as sound; 17:47 instead reports listening twice, then a private conference and an accusation of enchantment, and 17:48 continues with comparisons that leave their makers unable to find a way. The pericope thus places the obstruction in a burdened passage from hearing to acceptance and public interpretation.
findings.mechanism: The focus's ears and weight meet active listening in the next ayah, so simple acoustic absence is not the only available reading. Private exchange and the enchantment label supply a social reclassification; the immediate continuation's comparisons and loss of a way place that re-description beside disorientation. The sequence changes the reading from sound that never reaches them to sound that is heard and interpreted dismissively.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish hearing from accepting and see that the message's reception includes a social act of naming, followed by a loss of direction.
findings.containment: The focus noun still names ears and its weight remains an obstruction image. The adjacent sequence supports active listening and private characterization, but does not prove that the conference created the judgment or that the label caused the later loss of a way; the conference could report a settled view.

epistemic.reason: The focus and contexts supply the auditory, private-speech, accusation, and lost-way carriers; the directional social-recoding account remains attributed and its causal order is qualified.

findings.title: A present gate and a later response
findings.claim: The covers and ear-weight can sound like a fixed inability to respond; 17:52 places them beside a later divine call that receives an answer with praise. The focus therefore describes a present mode of resistant reception, while the pericope also presents a later response through the same hearing-and-answer channel.
findings.mechanism: The focus's burdened ears and flight meet 17:52's call, response, and praise. That later sequence changes the reading from permanent incapacity to a temporally situated gate, because response is shown elsewhere in the supplied pericope after a divine call.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold the focus's real resistance together with the later capacity to answer, without making either scene cancel the other.
findings.containment: The future response does not prove that the focus's hearers accept the present Quranic mention, and the later summons may be compelled rather than a reversal of moral stance. The temporal comparison remains attributed.

epistemic.reason: All trace coordinates and roots are represented in the supplied focus or context, but the claim that they describe one reception capacity across times remains an attributed HFT inference.

findings.title: A produced state under a split-root resonance
findings.claim: The focus's coverings remain coverings over hearts, yet its causative 'we made' can also frame them as a condition imposed on the hearers: 17:50's command to be stones or iron meets the focus through the packet's split mapping toward being and subjection. This moves the image, at an exploratory secondary level, from fixed objects alone to a produced state that constrains agency.
findings.mechanism: The focus's ja'ala branch describes bringing an existing participant into a new state; the covers and the attributed submission facet provide the focus carrier, while the separate k-w-n form in 17:50 supplies being-language as trigger. The shared mapped root ID connects distinct surface roots only through the supplied trace, so the contact suggests a state-image without making either focus word lexically mean submission.
findings.reader_payoff: The coverings can be seen as the hearers' condition as well as the objects in the focus image, while the ordinary image stays recoverable.
findings.containment: This is the packet's non-dominant, split-root mapping and remains attributed and exploratory. It does not establish lexical kinship between ك ن ن and ك و ن, make coverings mean subjection, or replace the ordinary reading; the context may simply be an unrelated command about resurrection.

epistemic.reason: The focus and 17:50 coordinates and their local roots agree with the supplied surfaces, but the semantic contact across the split mapping is weak and explicitly attributed.

findings.title: Withdrawal within encompassing lordship
findings.claim: The focus's turned backs and flight create real distance from the exclusive mention, while 17:60 says the Lord encompasses people. The withdrawal is therefore real at the level of the encounter but does not amount to escape from the encompassing relation named in the pericope.
findings.mechanism: The focus combines turning away, backs, and aversive flight into a directed movement; 17:60 independently supplies encompassing scope over people. The two meet so the spatial force of retreat is preserved yet bounded by a larger relation the movement cannot outrun.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the force of the flight without mistaking distance from the recitation for distance from divine encompassing.
findings.containment: The focus's withdrawal remains real; this overlay does not claim that the movement is physically stopped, that the hearers perceive the encompassing, or that the two ayat describe the same moment.

epistemic.reason: The focus movement and 17:60's encompassing verb are surface-grounded, while their relation as a limit on escape remains the attributed HFT reading.

findings.title: Exclusive mention and exclusive address
findings.claim: The focus's recoil when the Lord is mentioned alone gains a bounded external contrast: 1:2 names Allah as Lord of the worlds, and 1:5 then gives a plural speaker's address, 'You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help.' The Lord-alone relation that occasions recoil in the focus is thus also voiced as an affirmative address in the supplied Fātiḥa sequence.
findings.mechanism: The focus's Lord carrier meets the explicit Rabb occurrence in 1:2, which identifies the addressee of the following address; the focus's exclusivity then meets 1:5's repeated 'You alone'. These two individual external ayat connect the Lord named in the focus to a first-person plural confession of exclusive worship and help, changing the local report of recoil into a contrast of responses to exclusive divine address.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's aversion can be read beside a supplied voice that answers exclusive mention with worship and a request for help.
findings.containment: This overlay does not claim that 17:46 quotes Fātiḥa, that its historical addressees speak 1:5, or that the verses describe the same audience. Only the individually supplied 1:2 and 1:5 trigger the contrast; the native pericope reading stands without them.

epistemic.reason: The exact Arabic surfaces supply the Lord title and exclusive address, but their juxtaposition with the focus is an external overlay and the packet provides no word-level QAC analysis for these added ayat.
